name: Inugami (S-Class Bloodragers Bloodline)
body:
You were born with a terrible curse. When your soul would pass into the Realms of Death, it will instead be consumed by the inugami; dog-like spirits that exist on the edge of dreams and at the corners of tired eyes, ready to pounce.

You fight to avoid that fate, drawing on your curse for power in times of need.

Bloodline Feats Combat Casting, Diehard, Endurance, Iron Will, Skill Focus (survival), Spell Focus, Still Spell, Toughness

Bloodline Spells keen senses (7th), ghost wolf (10th), greater magic fang (13th), summon monster IV (dog-like creatures only, 17th)

Saving Throws

Any saving throw DCs associated with your bloodline powers are equal to 10 + 1/2 your bloodrager level + your Charisma modifier

Sharpened Canines (Su)

While using bloodrage, you gain a natural bite attack, dealing piercing damage equivalent to that of a creature normal for your size (1d4 for Small races, 1d6 for Medium, etc…). This bite adds twice your Strength modifier to damage and has a x3 critical multiplier. It is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if you are also wielding manufactured weapons.

If you have a magic weapon in your possession, but are not wielding it, you can apply the magic properties of that weapon to your bite, if it meets their prerequisites (it can’t gain the disruption ability, for example).

Satiate (Su)

At 4th level, whenever you hit a creature with your bite attack, you can regain hit points equal to half the damage dealt (up to your max hp) as a free action. You can regain hit points up to a maximum of 5 x your bloodrager level each day in this way.

Guard Dog (Su)

At 8th level, you gain a +1 luck bonus on all of your saving throws and to your AC during surprise rounds and when you are otherwise unaware of an attack. At 14th level, and again at 20th level, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +3 at 20th level.

Ravenous (Sp)

At 12th level, you can cast haste, targeting yourself, at will when you enter a bloodrage. This doesn’t expend a spell slot, but each round spent in bloodrage counts as 2 until it ends.

Not Yet Time (Sp)

Once per day at 16th level, when you are using bloodrage and would be reduced to 0 or fewer hit points, but not killed outright or destroyed, you remain staggered at 1 hit point instead. This lasts until the end of your next turn, even if you would take additional damage. If you aren’t healed to positive hit points at the end of your next turn, you become subject to your current condition as normal.

Feed the Curse (Sp)

Once per day at 20th level, if you would die or be destroyed, you can expend all remaining rounds of bloodrage (minimum 1) and all remaining spell slots to cast magic jar as an immediate action (Will negates). If you successfully possess the target, it dies instead, and your body reforms in its place, wearing any of its equipment that would fit you (the rest falls to the ground at your feet).
